newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's 1996 inflation 11.84 pct vs 10.23 in 1995.
newsitem.headline: Peru's 1996 inflation 11.84 pct vs 10.23 in 1995.

text.p: Consumer prices in Peru rose 11.84 percent in 1996, compared with a 10.23 percent rise last year, the government said Tuesday.

Consumer prices in December rose 1.2 percent, compared with a 0.5 percent rise in the same month last year and 0.7 percent in November 1996, the National Statistics and Information Institute (INEI) said.
Consumer inflation fell to 10.2 percent in 1995 from 15.4 percent the previous year. The 1995 figure was the lowest in 23 years.
The government originally aimed for single-digit inflation this year and later agreed to a target of between 9.5 percent and 11.5 percent with the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
The government's budget predicts nine percent inflation in 1997.
